checklist.step: Open the market-entry request and pin the exact state and line scope
actions: Take the signed market-entry request from the Insurance Product Manager and open a case named <writing company>-SC-<target first-write date>.
Record on the case: writing company legal name and NAIC company code, target state (South Carolina), target first-write date, distribution channel, and the products to be sold.
Ask the Chief Underwriting Officer for the coverage grants each product carries so the line scope is drawn from policy language, not from the marketing name.
List every state/line pair the entry needs on the case, one row per pair, and mark whether it is new business only or new plus assumed in-force.
checklist.done: the case carries the writing company, NAIC code, target date and a one-row-per-state/line scope list agreed with underwriting.

checklist.step: Pull the current Certificate of Authority of record for the state
actions: Open the CoA register folder for the writing company and retrieve the most recent South Carolina Certificate of Authority PDF and any amendment endorsements.
Read the face of the CoA and transcribe verbatim the kinds of insurance authorised and the effective date onto the case.
Check the CoA has not been suspended, restricted or made conditional by a later SC DOI order held in the same folder.
Where the repository copy is older than the last corporate amendment, request a certified copy from the SC DOI Company Licensing section and note the request date.
checklist.done: the case holds the current, unrestricted SC CoA with its authorised kinds of insurance transcribed word for word.

checklist.step: Map each product coverage to South Carolina's statutory line-of-insurance codes
actions: Open SC Code Title 38 Chapter 1 and Chapter 9 and list the statutory kinds of insurance SC recognises (fire, casualty, marine, surety, life, accident and health, title and so on).
For each product coverage grant, name the single statutory kind it falls under and write the SC label plus the NAIC annual statement line number on the scope row.
Send hybrid or packaged coverages to Regulatory Counsel for a written call rather than choosing the closest fit.
Compare the mapped kinds against the transcribed CoA face and mark each scope row COVERED or GAP.
checklist.done: every scope row shows an SC statutory kind, an annual statement line number, and a COVERED or GAP verdict.

checklist.step: Confirm admitted status and authorised lines independently at the source
actions: In NAIC iSite+ open the company profile for the NAIC company code and read the Licensing/State Licenses view for South Carolina.
Open the SC Department of Insurance online company search and look up the company by NAIC code, then screenshot the lines-of-authority panel with the date visible.
Compare the iSite+ lines, the SC DOI lines and the paper CoA face; any three-way difference is investigated with SC DOI Company Licensing before the case proceeds.
File both captures in the case folder as <SC>-authority-verification-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf.
checklist.done: iSite+, the SC DOI company search and the paper CoA agree on the authorised lines, with dated captures on file.

checklist.step: Choose the authority route for every GAP row
actions: For each GAP row select one route: UCAA Expansion Application (company not admitted in SC), UCAA Corporate Amendments Application (admitted but the kind is not on the CoA), surplus lines placement through a licensed SC surplus lines broker, or drop the line from the entry.
Write the statutory basis for the route onto the row, citing the SC Code section relied on.
Where surplus lines is chosen, confirm the risk is eligible under SC's diligent-search and export-list rules and record who will file the SC premium tax through the surplus lines stamping process.
Sign and date the route decision on each GAP row - an unrouted GAP row blocks the whole entry.
checklist.done: every GAP row has a counsel-signed route with an SC Code citation, or the line is removed from the entry scope.

checklist.step: Assemble the UCAA package for the chosen route
actions: Download the current UCAA Expansion or Corporate Amendments checklist for South Carolina from the NAIC UCAA page and print it to the case folder with the date visible.

Assemble each numbered item the checklist demands: Uniform Application form, Form 1 Uniform Consent to Service of Process, certified charter and bylaws, the state-of-domicile Certificate of Compliance, audited statutory financials, plan of operation with three-year pro-formas, and NAIC Form 11 biographical affidavits with third-party verification for each officer and director.

Chase HR and the Corporate Secretary for the officer/director list so no biographical affidavit is missed, and check every affidavit verification report is dated within the SC-accepted staleness window (three years is the working assumption).
Tick each checklist line as it is satisfied and leave a note on any item SC waives, quoting the waiver source.
checklist.done: every line of the dated SC UCAA checklist is ticked or waived with a quoted source, and the package is assembled in checklist order.

checklist.step: Prove the capital, surplus and deposit tests South Carolina applies
actions: Read the minimum capital and surplus figures SC Code Title 38 Chapter 9 sets for each kind of insurance in scope and note the highest applicable figure.
Pull capital and surplus from the latest filed Annual Statement page 3 and the most recent quarterly, and compute headroom against the SC minimum.
Confirm any statutory deposit SC requires is lodged and get the custodian's confirmation letter into the package.
Where headroom is under 20%, notify the Chief Financial Officer before filing so the plan of operation pro-formas are defensible.
checklist.done: capital, surplus and any required deposit clear the SC minimum with the computation and custodian letter in the package.

checklist.step: Submit the UCAA filing to the SC Department of Insurance and open the clock
actions: Submit the package by the route the SC UCAA checklist specifies (SC accepts electronic submission through the NAIC UCAA electronic filing option; use paper only where the checklist demands it) and pay the SC application and licence fees named on the checklist.
Record on the case: submission date, method, fee amount, payment reference and the SC DOI analyst assigned.
Set the expected decision date at submission date plus the SC review window used for planning (90 days) and load it into the CoA register with T-60 and T-30 alerts.
Send the Insurance Product Manager a written earliest-possible-write date so launch planning stops assuming the original target.
checklist.done: the filing is lodged with a dated receipt, fee reference and an expected decision date loaded into the register with alerts.

checklist.step: Clear SC DOI deficiency letters without letting the clock run out
actions: Log each SC DOI deficiency or objection letter on the case within one business day of receipt with the reply-by date the letter states.
Allocate every numbered deficiency to a named owner in Finance, Actuarial, HR or Legal with an internal due date five business days before the state's reply-by date.
Draft the response referencing the deficiency numbers, attach the cured documents, and keep a copy of the outbound response in the case folder.
Where a deficiency cannot be cured, take the withdraw-and-refile decision to the Head of Compliance rather than letting the filing be denied on the record.
checklist.done: every deficiency has an owner, a dated response filed before the state's reply-by date, and a copy in the case.

checklist.step: Book the issued Certificate of Authority into the register
actions: On receipt, read the issued SC CoA and confirm the authorised kinds match the scope list line for line - a partial grant is treated as a GAP, not a win.
Create the register entry: state, writing company, NAIC code, CoA number, issue date, authorised kinds, annual continuation fee amount and anniversary date.
Upload the CoA PDF and the SC DOI approval letter to the repository under <company>/CoA/SC and link them to the register entry.
Circulate the issued authority to Underwriting, Policy Administration, Actuarial and the Producer Compliance Manager in one written notice.
checklist.done: the register carries a complete SC entry linked to the CoA PDF, and the authority notice has gone to underwriting, policy admin and licensing.

checklist.step: Turn the Certificate of Authority into enforced system write authority
actions: Open the underwriting appetite and authority tables and enable South Carolina only for the statutory kinds the issued CoA names.
Set the enablement effective date to the CoA effective date so no quote can be dated earlier.
Have a Senior Underwriter attempt a test quote in an SC line that is not on the CoA and confirm the platform refuses it.
Record the configuration change reference and the failed test-quote screenshot on the market-entry case.
checklist.done: SC is enabled only for CoA-named kinds from the CoA effective date, evidenced by a refused out-of-authority test quote.

checklist.step: Set the hard bind block in policy administration
actions: Configure the state/line authority matrix so a bind attempt for an SC state/line pair with no CoA entry fails with a blocking message naming the CoA gap.
Point the matrix at the CoA register as its source so a withdrawn or suspended CoA closes the state automatically.
Run the regression pack over one covered and one uncovered SC line and attach both results to the change record.
Give Production Support the runbook for the block message so a genuine gap is never bypassed at the service desk.
checklist.done: policy admin blocks binds for uncovered SC state/line pairs, sourced from the register, with regression evidence attached.

checklist.step: Hand the authority into the producer licensing and appointment chain
actions: Confirm on nipr.com that the writing company's SC company record and NAIC code are set up for appointment transactions before any producer is appointed.
Give the Producer Licensing Coordinator the CoA-authorised lines so SC appointments are only submitted for lines of authority the company itself can write.
Block appointment submission for any SC line of authority outside the CoA in the agency/producer management system rules.
Confirm in writing to Distribution that no SC solicitation begins before both the CoA effective date and the first confirmed producer appointment.
checklist.done: SC appointments can only be raised for CoA-authorised lines and distribution has the written no-solicit-before date.

checklist.step: Keep the Certificate of Authority alive year on year
actions: Diary the SC continuation fee against the anniversary date on the register and pay it with a 45-day reminder and a 15-day escalation.
File a UCAA Corporate Amendments Application whenever the company changes name, redomesticates, changes control, or adds a kind of insurance - and before, not after, the change is used in SC.
Refresh the register entry after every amendment and re-run the underwriting and policy-admin authority configuration.
At each March 1 Schedule T filing, tie premium written in SC to the register and raise any state/line pair with premium but no authority as an immediate exception.
checklist.done: continuation fees are paid on time, amendments are filed before use, and Schedule T ties to the register each year.

checklist.step: File the market-entry evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the complete case folder - scope list, line mapping, dated authority captures, UCAA package, deficiency correspondence, issued CoA and system configuration evidence - into the repository under writing company and state.
Apply the 10-years-from-withdrawal retention label so the record outlives any decision to exit South Carolina.
Confirm the record is indexed and retrievable by NAIC company code, state, CoA number and statutory kind.
Record the repository reference back on the market-entry case and close it.
checklist.done: the market-entry record is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by NAIC code, state and CoA number.

testing.step: Build the premium-by-state-and-line population
actions: Extract every policy with an effective date in the period, carrying writing company, NAIC code, risk state, statutory line and written premium.
Add assumed reinsurance and program business written on the company's paper so business placed through third parties cannot hide.
Summarise to one row per writing company, state and statutory line and record the row and premium totals in the workpaper.
Have the extract signed as complete by the person who ran it, with the query and run date attached.
testing.done: a signed, query-documented population of premium by writing company, state and statutory line exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to Schedule T
actions: Pull Schedule T direct written premium by state from the filed Annual Statement in iSite+ for the same writing company and year.
Compare the extract's premium by state to Schedule T and list every state whose difference exceeds 1% or $100,000.
Chase each difference to a cause with the Statutory Reporting Manager (timing, cancellations, allocation of multistate risks) and clear it before sampling.
An unexplained state on Schedule T with no extract premium is treated as a scope failure, not a rounding item.
testing.done: premium by state ties to Schedule T within tolerance and every remaining difference has a documented cause.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of state/line pairs opened for the first time in the period, and 100% of pairs whose premium is under $50,000 (new or fringe lines are where authority gaps live).
Take 25 further pairs at random from the remainder using a recorded seed, for a minimum of 40 pairs in total.
Record population size, seed, selection date and the selection rule in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn identically.
List South Carolina pairs separately as the representative-jurisdiction subsample.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of at least 40 state/line pairs is drawn, covering every newly opened pair.

testing.step: Re-perform the authority lookup at source for each sampled pair
actions: For each sampled pair, open the NAIC iSite+ company licensing view and the relevant state DOI company search and read the authorised kinds without opening the CoA register first.
Reach an independent covered/not-covered conclusion, then compare it to the register entry - a match on outcome with a wrong CoA number or effective date is still an exception.
For the South Carolina pairs, read the issued CoA face against SC Code Title 38 Chapter 9 kinds rather than relying on the internal label.
Capture each source screen with the date visible into the workpaper against the sample row.
testing.done: each sampled pair has an independent authority conclusion with a dated source capture and a documented comparison.

testing.step: Test the statutory line-code mapping behind the register
actions: For 10 sampled products, read the policy form coverage grants and map them yourself to the state's statutory kinds and the annual statement line number.
Compare to the mapping recorded on the market-entry case; flag any product mapped to a broader kind than its coverage grant supports.
Give special attention to packaged and hybrid products, warranty-like coverages and any product carrying an inland marine or surety element.
Record disagreements as mapping exceptions with the coverage wording quoted.
testing.done: 10 product mappings are independently re-performed and every disagreement is logged with the coverage wording quoted.

testing.step: Trace each newly opened pair back to a filed UCAA package and approval
actions: For every pair opened in the period, retrieve the UCAA package, the dated state checklist, the fee payment reference and the state approval letter.
Confirm the approval letter pre-dates the earliest policy effective date for that pair, and record both dates side by side.
Check the biographical affidavits and Certificate of Compliance in the package carry dates inside the state's staleness window at submission.
Any pair with premium but no approval letter is escalated immediately, not carried to the end of the test.
testing.done: every newly opened pair has an approval letter pre-dating its first policy, with both dates recorded.

testing.step: Prove the system bind block actually enforces the register
actions: In the test environment attempt to bind an SC risk in a statutory kind absent from the CoA and confirm the transaction is refused with the authority message.
Suspend a test state/line entry in the register copy and confirm the block engages downstream without a manual configuration change.
Read the change history on the authority matrix for the period and list every manual override, with who applied it and why.
Any override applied without a Regulatory Affairs Manager approval is an exception regardless of whether premium resulted.
testing.done: the block refuses out-of-authority SC binds, follows the register automatically, and every override is approved and explained.

testing.step: Recompute the continuation and amendment deadline maths
actions: For 15 register entries, recompute the continuation fee due date from the CoA anniversary date and compare it to the payment date on the finance record.
For each corporate change in the period (name, control, redomestication, added kind), compare the amendment filing date to the date the change was first used in the market.
Recompute the planned earliest-write date as submission date plus the state review window and compare it to the actual first policy effective date.
Any use before approval, or any continuation fee paid after the anniversary, is a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: continuation and amendment dates reconcile, and no state/line pair was used before its approval date.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying writing company, state, statutory line, premium at risk, policy count and what was missed.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (mapping error, register not updated, amendment filed late, block overridden, entry bypassed the gate) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date, and for unauthorized-writing exceptions open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and decide on rescission, non-renewal or fronting.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's sweep as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where premium was written, a counsel self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute the exception rate and premium at risk and compare against the zero-unauthorized-premium threshold.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who neither maintains the register nor prepared any sampled UCAA filing, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the result, open breaches and self-report decisions to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, exception rate and premium at risk, and the committee reporting date is recorded.

checklist.step: Take in the Alabama producer or agency onboarding request
actions: Open the onboarding queue filtered to State = Alabama and Status = New request and create a producer record.
Capture from the recruiting Agency Relations Manager: legal name exactly as licensed, National Producer Number, resident state, agency affiliation, intended products and intended writing lines.
Reject the request back to the recruiter where the NPN is missing rather than searching on name alone, because name-only matches pull the wrong producer.
Set the record status to Pending verification and stamp the request date, which starts the onboarding clock.
checklist.done: a producer record exists carrying NPN, legal name, resident state, agency and intended Alabama lines, stamped with the request date.

checklist.step: Pull the Alabama licence picture from the NIPR Producer Database
actions: Sign in to the NIPR Gateway and run a PDB Report on the NPN, selecting Alabama in the state licence section.
Read and transcribe onto the record: Alabama licence number, licence class (individual or business entity), resident/non-resident status, original issue date, expiration date and licence status.
Confirm the status reads Active - a status of Inactive, Expired, Suspended, Revoked or Pending is a hard stop, not a follow-up item.
Save the PDB report to the producer record as PDB-<NPN>-AL-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf; this dated capture is the evidence the verification happened before contracting.
checklist.done: a dated Alabama PDB report is attached and the record carries licence number, class, status and expiration date.

checklist.step: Match Alabama lines of authority to the products the producer will sell
actions: List the Alabama lines of authority on the PDB report (Life, Accident and Health or Sickness, Property, Casualty, Personal Lines, Variable Life and Variable Annuity and so on).
Set against them the products the producer is being appointed to sell and mark each product MATCHED or UNMATCHED.
For variable products, confirm the FINRA registration and the Variable Life/Variable Annuity LOA are both present before the product is allowed.
Where a product is UNMATCHED, either remove the product from the producer's authorised list or send them to obtain the LOA before contracting - never appoint on the expectation of a future LOA.
checklist.done: every product on the producer's authorised list maps to an Alabama LOA held today, with unmatched products removed.

checklist.step: Read the regulatory action history before you contract
actions: In the same PDB report open the Regulatory Actions (RIRS) section and read every action across all states, not only Alabama.
For each action record the state, action date, reason code and disposition, and pull the underlying consent order where the reason involves fraud, misappropriation of premium or unlicensed activity.
Refer any action involving dishonesty or breach of trust to the 1033 consent screening before the file moves on.
Write a documented accept, accept-with-conditions or decline recommendation onto the record and have the Producer Compliance Manager countersign it.
checklist.done: every RIRS action is read and dispositioned, with a countersigned accept/decline recommendation on the record.

checklist.step: Verify the agency licence and its designated responsible licensed producer
actions: Where the producer writes through an agency, run a separate PDB report on the agency's own NPN and FEIN.
Confirm the Alabama business-entity licence is active and carries the lines of authority the agency's producers will write.
Identify the designated responsible licensed producer named on the agency licence and confirm that individual holds a current Alabama licence.
Attach both PDB reports and record the agency licence number and DRLP name on the agency record.
checklist.done: the agency's Alabama entity licence and its DRLP are both verified active with dated PDB reports attached.

checklist.step: Route non-resident producers through NIPR non-resident licensing first
actions: For a producer whose home state is not Alabama, confirm the home-state licence is Active in PDB, since Alabama non-resident status collapses when the home state lapses.

Where no Alabama non-resident licence exists, submit the Non-Resident Licensing application on the NIPR Gateway with the NPN, home-state licence and the requested Alabama LOAs, and pay the Alabama licence fee.
Track the application to issuance and re-pull the PDB report to confirm the Alabama licence number and status before contracting.
Note on the record that a home-state lapse cancels the Alabama non-resident licence, so the PDB alert must cover the home state too.
checklist.done: non-resident producers hold an issued, PDB-confirmed Alabama licence with the home-state licence confirmed active.

checklist.step: Hold solicitation closed until verification passes
actions: Keep the producer's CRM user in a no-territory, no-lead state until the producer record shows Verified for Alabama.
Configure lead assignment so an Alabama lead cannot be routed to a producer without an active Alabama LOA covering that lead's product.
Withhold Broker and Agent Portal quoting entitlements for Alabama until the verification and appointment flags are both set.
Send the recruiter a written statement that pre-appointment prospecting, quoting and application-taking in Alabama are prohibited.
checklist.done: the producer holds no Alabama leads, territory or quoting entitlement until the verified and appointed flags are both set.

checklist.step: Execute the producer agreement only after verification
actions: Send the Alabama producer agreement for signature only once the record shows a dated PDB verification.
Include in the agreement the licence and appointment covenants, the commission-forfeiture clause for unlicensed activity, and the duty to report regulatory actions within 30 days.
Record the envelope completion date on the producer record - this date starts the statutory appointment window.
File the executed agreement against the producer record and notify the Producer Licensing Coordinator to raise the appointment.
checklist.done: the agreement is executed after a dated verification and the completion date is recorded as the appointment-window start.

checklist.step: Submit the Alabama appointment through the NIPR Gateway
actions: In the NIPR Gateway open Electronic Appointments and start an appointment submission for Alabama.
Enter the writing company's NAIC company code, the producer NPN, the appointment effective date and only the lines of authority the CoA and the producer's licence both support.
Submit within 15 days of the earlier of the agreement execution date or the producer's first submitted Alabama application, and pay the Alabama appointment fee.
Record the NIPR transaction reference and submission date on the producer record.
checklist.done: an Alabama appointment is submitted inside the 15-day window with the NIPR transaction reference recorded.

checklist.step: Confirm the appointment landed and clear rejects the same week
actions: Retrieve the NIPR transaction status report the next business day and confirm the Alabama appointment shows Accepted.
Work every reject to its stated reason code - wrong company code, LOA not held, licence expired, duplicate appointment - and resubmit within the original 15-day window.
Re-pull the PDB report and confirm the appointment now appears under the writing company with the correct effective date.
Attach the acceptance confirmation to the producer record and set the record status to Appointed.
checklist.done: the appointment shows Accepted in NIPR and on a re-pulled PDB report, with the confirmation attached.

checklist.step: Open writing numbers and commission eligibility only on the appointed flag
actions: Create the Alabama writing number with an effective date no earlier than the appointment effective date confirmed in NIPR.
Set commission eligibility to key off the appointed flag on the producer master so a lapse suspends payment automatically.
Configure the platform to reject commission on any Alabama policy whose application date pre-dates the appointment effective date.
Send Distribution the first-payable date so no advance or draw is issued against unappointed production.
checklist.done: the Alabama writing number and commission eligibility start no earlier than the confirmed appointment effective date.

checklist.step: Subscribe the producer to ongoing NIPR status monitoring
actions: Add the NPN to the NIPR PDB Alerts subscription for Alabama and for the producer's home state.
Configure alert delivery into the licensing work queue so a status change creates a case rather than an unread email.
Define the standing response: an Expired, Suspended or Revoked alert suspends the writing number and CRM entitlements the same business day.
Record the subscription reference on the producer record so the monitoring can be evidenced at exam.
checklist.done: the NPN is under PDB Alerts for Alabama and the home state, with alerts landing in the licensing queue as cases.

checklist.step: Wire the producer into the policy administration writing hierarchy
actions: Load the producer's NPN, Alabama licence number, LOAs and appointment effective date onto the policy admin producer master from the agency/producer management system, not by hand.
Configure the new-business edit so an Alabama application is refused when the writing NPN has no active licence and appointment for that product's LOA on the application date.
Run the refusal test with an expired test NPN and attach the result to the configuration change record.
Confirm the daily producer-master feed runs so a status change in NIPR reaches the bind gate within one business day.
checklist.done: policy admin refuses Alabama applications from unlicensed or unappointed NPNs, fed daily from the producer master.

checklist.step: Brief the producer on what they may and may not do in Alabama
actions: Assign the Alabama pre-appointment conduct module covering solicitation boundaries, LOA limits, the duty to report regulatory actions within 30 days and the CE and renewal obligations.
Require completion before the CRM entitlement is released and record the completion date on the producer record.
Send the producer the written list of the products and LOAs they are authorised to solicit in Alabama.
Diary an annual refresh tied to the producer's licence expiration month.
checklist.done: the producer has completed the Alabama conduct module and holds a written list of authorised products and LOAs.

checklist.step: File the verification and appointment evidence
actions: Move the producer file - dated PDB reports, LOA match sheet, RIRS disposition, executed agreement, NIPR appointment confirmation and training record - into the repository under the writing company and state.
Apply the 5-years-after-termination retention label so the file survives the producer leaving.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, Alabama licence number and appointment effective date.
Write the repository reference onto the producer record and close the onboarding case.
checklist.done: the producer file is retained for 5 years after termination and retrievable by NPN and Alabama licence number.

testing.step: Build the Alabama application and producer population
actions: Extract every Alabama new-business application and bound policy in the quarter with application date, bind date, product, LOA and writing producer NPN.
Extract from the agency/producer management system every producer and agency with an Alabama status change in the quarter.
Reject rows with a blank or malformed NPN into a separate list - a missing NPN is itself an exception, not a data cleanse.
Record both populations with row counts, query text and run date, signed by the extractor.
testing.done: a signed population of Alabama applications and onboarded producers exists, with blank-NPN rows separately listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the commission and CRM records
actions: Pull Alabama commission payments for the quarter by NPN and join them to the application population.
List any NPN paid commission with no application in the population, and any application with no producer master record.
Chase each difference with the Commission Analyst and clear it before sampling - a paid NPN absent from the roster is investigated as a possible unlicensed writer.
Record the reconciliation and its residual differences in the workpaper.
testing.done: commission-paid NPNs and application NPNs reconcile to the producer roster, with residual differences explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers onboarded to Alabama in the quarter and 100% of NPNs carrying a RIRS action.
Take 40 applications at random from the remaining population using a recorded seed, weighted to the first 30 days after each producer's appointment date.
Record population size, seed, weighting rule and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Separate variable-product applications into their own subsample because they carry the extra FINRA and variable LOA test.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering every new Alabama onboarding and 40 applications is drawn and documented.

testing.step: Re-pull the Producer Database for each sampled NPN as at the application date
actions: Run a fresh PDB report on each sampled NPN and read the Alabama licence history, including original issue, renewal and any lapse periods.
Determine independently whether the licence was Active on the application date, without opening the stored verification first.
Compare your conclusion to the stored PDB capture; a stored capture dated after the contract execution date is an exception even when the licence was in fact active.
Attach each fresh PDB report to the sample row.
testing.done: each sampled NPN has an independent licence-status conclusion as at its application date with a fresh PDB attached.

testing.step: Re-perform the line-of-authority match
actions: For each sampled application, read the product sold and name the Alabama LOA it requires from Title 27 Chapter 7 definitions.
Compare that LOA to the LOAs held on the re-pulled PDB report as at the application date.
Test variable products separately: both the Variable Life/Variable Annuity LOA and a current FINRA registration must be present.
Log any application sold on an LOA the producer did not hold as a fail, and quantify the premium and commission attached to it.
testing.done: every sampled application is matched to a held LOA, or logged as a fail with premium and commission quantified.

testing.step: Trace the appointment to a NIPR transaction that pre-dates the business
actions: For each sampled NPN, retrieve the NIPR appointment transaction confirmation and read the submission date, effective date and accepted lines.
Confirm the appointment effective date is on or before the earliest sampled application date for that producer.
Confirm the appointment is recorded against the correct writing company NAIC code - an appointment under a sister company does not cover this paper.
Capture the NIPR transaction screen and the PDB appointment section into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled producer has an accepted Alabama appointment under the correct NAIC code, effective before their first application.

testing.step: Recompute the 15-day appointment window
actions: For each onboarded producer, take the earlier of the agreement execution date and the first submitted Alabama application date as day zero.
Recompute day zero plus 15 days and compare it to the NIPR submission date recorded on the transaction confirmation.
List every submission beyond day 15 with the number of days late and the applications written inside the gap.
Confirm the onboarding queue alerts at day 5 and day 10 actually fired for each late case, or record the monitoring failure alongside the breach.
testing.done: the 15-day window is recomputed for every onboarding, with days late and gap applications listed for each breach.

testing.step: Test the solicitation and bind gates independently
actions: In the test environment assign an Alabama lead to a producer with no Alabama LOA and confirm the CRM refuses the assignment.
Attempt an Alabama application in policy administration under an expired test NPN and confirm the new-business edit refuses it.
Read the override log on both gates for the quarter, listing who overrode, for which NPN and on what stated grounds.
Confirm the daily producer-master feed ran on every business day in the quarter; a missed feed day is a control gap even with no resulting exception.
testing.done: both gates refuse unlicensed producers in test, and every override and feed failure in the quarter is listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, producer name, application numbers, premium, commission paid and what was missed.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (verification skipped, appointment filed late, LOA mismatch, PDB alert not worked, gate overridden) and a named owner.
For unlicensed or unappointed writing, decide with Regulatory Counsel on commission clawback, policyholder notification, and whether an Alabama DOI self-report is required.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a counsel decision on clawback and self-report.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold and quantify premium and commission written by unlicensed or unappointed producers.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the Internal Auditor, who processes no appointments and performed none of the sampled verifications, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report results, breaches and self-report decisions to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, exception rate and unlicensed premium, with a recorded committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Detect the appointment trigger the moment it happens
actions: Run the daily trigger report that lists SC producer agreements completed in DocuSign yesterday and SC applications submitted by producers with no active appointment.
Open an appointment case per trigger recording NPN, producer name, trigger type (agreement executed or first application), trigger date and the products involved.
Set day zero on the case to the earlier of the two trigger dates - not the date the case was opened, which is the mistake that eats the window.
Escalate any first-application trigger to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day, because business is already on the books unappointed.
checklist.done: every SC trigger has a case with day zero set to the earlier of agreement execution and first application date.

checklist.step: Compute and publish the statutory due date on the case
actions: Compute the appointment due date as day zero plus 15 calendar days and write it on the case as the statutory due date.
Set the internal working target three business days earlier to leave room for a NIPR reject and resubmission.
Load the case into the licensing queue with automatic alerts at day 5 and day 10 and an escalation to the Producer Compliance Manager at day 12.
Where day zero is already more than 15 days past, mark the case Late on creation so it is never quietly filed as on time.
checklist.done: each case shows a computed day-15 statutory due date, an earlier internal target, and live day 5/10/12 alerts.

checklist.step: Confirm the licence and lines still support the appointment
actions: Run a fresh PDB report on the NPN for South Carolina and confirm the licence status is Active on the intended appointment effective date.
List the SC lines of authority held and strike from the appointment request any line the producer does not hold.
Confirm the writing company holds SC authority for each requested line from the Certificate of Authority register before the line is submitted.
Attach the dated PDB report to the case as the pre-submission verification.
checklist.done: the SC licence is confirmed active and every requested line is held by both the producer and the writing company.

checklist.step: Submit the South Carolina appointment through NIPR
actions: In the NIPR Gateway open Electronic Appointments, select South Carolina and the writing company's NAIC company code, and enter the NPN, appointment effective date and lines of authority.
Set the appointment effective date to day zero, not to today, so the record shows the producer appointed from the date business could first be written.
Submit and pay the SC appointment fee, then record the NIPR transaction reference, submission date and fee amount on the case.
Where SC requires the transaction through State Based Systems for a particular scenario, follow that route and record the SBS confirmation instead.
checklist.done: the SC appointment is submitted inside the window with the transaction reference, effective date and fee recorded.

checklist.step: Work the NIPR rejects before the window closes
actions: Download the NIPR transaction status report each business morning and open every SC reject.
Fix by reason code: correct the NAIC company code, remove a line of authority not held, resolve an expired licence with the producer, or clear a duplicate appointment already on file.
Resubmit the same business day and keep the original day-zero effective date on the resubmission.
Where a reject cannot be cleared before day 15, escalate to the Producer Compliance Manager and stop the producer from writing further SC business.
checklist.done: every SC reject is worked the same business day and either resubmitted or escalated with SC writing stopped.

checklist.step: Renew South Carolina appointments in the annual renewal cycle
actions: When the SC appointment renewal invoice is published, download the invoiced producer list from the NIPR Gateway and load it into the renewal worksheet.
Reconcile the invoice line by line to the active SC producer roster: mark each as renew, or as terminate-before-billing where the producer is no longer writing.
Send the terminate list through the termination process before the renewal payment date so the company is not billed for producers it will terminate weeks later.
Authorise payment for the renew list, then confirm on a re-pulled PDB report that each renewed appointment shows the new expiration.
checklist.done: the SC renewal invoice is reconciled to the roster, non-writers are terminated first, and renewals confirm on PDB.

checklist.step: Take in the termination trigger from any source
actions: Accept termination triggers from four sources and log each with its source: Distribution (contract cancelled), HR (employed agent leaves), Compliance (conduct finding) and the annual renewal reconciliation (inactive producer).
Open a termination case recording NPN, SC appointment effective date, termination effective date, the requesting party and the stated reason.
Set day zero to the termination effective date and compute the state notice due date as day zero plus 30 calendar days.
Suspend the producer's SC writing entitlement immediately on case creation rather than waiting for the filing.
checklist.done: each termination has a case with source, termination effective date, a computed day-30 due date and writing suspended.

checklist.step: Decide the termination reason code before anything is filed
actions: Run the reason-code decision tree: not for cause (voluntary, retirement, no production, book moved) versus for cause (violation of insurance law, fraud, misappropriation of premium, forgery, misrepresentation, conviction, licence action).
Where any for-cause indicator is present, gather the underlying evidence file - complaint records, audit findings, premium trust account shortfall, SIU referral - before selecting the code.
Never default to not for cause to avoid a difficult narrative; a knowingly wrong code is the failure the statute is aimed at.
Record the selected NAIC reason code, the reasoning and the evidence references on the case and sign it.
checklist.done: a signed reason-code determination with supporting evidence references sits on the case before any filing.

checklist.step: Have counsel clear every for-cause narrative
actions: Read the evidence file behind each for-cause termination and confirm the facts stated are ones the company can support if the producer contests them.
Draft the narrative to state facts and the reason code only, with no speculation, so the statutory immunity for good-faith reporting is not put at risk.
Confirm with the Producer Compliance Manager whether the same facts also require a separate SIU, fidelity bond or fraud-bureau report.
Sign and date the cleared narrative onto the case.
checklist.done: every for-cause narrative is counsel-cleared, fact-only and dated before submission.

checklist.step: File the termination notice with the SC Director inside 30 days
actions: In the NIPR Gateway open Terminations, select South Carolina and the writing company NAIC code, and enter the NPN, termination effective date and the cleared reason code.
Attach or enter the for-cause narrative where the code requires it, using the counsel-cleared text verbatim.
Submit on or before day 30 from the termination effective date and record the transaction reference and submission date on the case.
Confirm acceptance on the next business day's NIPR status report and re-pull the PDB to see the appointment closed.
checklist.done: the SC termination is accepted in NIPR on or before day 30 with the cleared reason code and narrative recorded.

checklist.step: Send the producer their copy inside 15 days of notifying the Director
actions: Generate the producer copy of the termination notice, reproducing the information filed with the Director including the reason code.
Send it to the producer's last known address of record from the PDB report by a method that evidences delivery, and to their record email.
Compute the due date as the NIPR submission date plus 15 calendar days and confirm the send date falls inside it.
File the copy, the address source and the proof of sending on the termination case.
checklist.done: the producer copy is sent to the PDB address of record within 15 days of the state filing, with proof of sending on file.

checklist.step: Answer any SC Director request for supplementary information
actions: Log any SC DOI request for additional information on a filed termination on the day of receipt with the 30-day response due date.
Assemble the documents and information the request names, working with SIU, Internal Audit or Distribution as the facts require.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the response package before it leaves, again keeping to facts and documents.
File the outbound response and the delivery evidence on the termination case and record the response date.
checklist.done: every supplementary-information request is answered inside 30 days with a counsel-reviewed, filed response.

checklist.step: Shut off downstream access, commissions and orphan exposure
actions: Close the SC writing number effective the termination effective date and stop new-business commission from that date.
Decide and record the renewal-commission treatment under the producer agreement (vested, forfeited on for-cause, or held pending investigation) and apply it.
Revoke CRM, Broker and Agent Portal and policy administration access the same business day and confirm the revocation with the IAM team.
Give Distribution the terminated producer's in-force book so orphaned SC policyholders are reassigned to an appointed servicing producer.
checklist.done: the writing number is closed, commission treatment applied, access revoked and the orphan book reassigned.

checklist.step: Age the open cases every day and escalate what is slipping
actions: Open the daily ageing view of SC appointment and termination cases, sorted by days remaining to the statutory due date.
Reassign any case with fewer than three days remaining and personally clear cases already past due the same day.
Raise a tracker exception for each case that passed its statutory date, recording the days late and the cause before it is filed.
Report the weekly count of at-risk and late cases to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: no SC case reaches its statutory date unworked, and every late case is logged with days late and cause.

checklist.step: Retain the appointment and termination evidence
actions: Move each closed case - trigger record, PDB captures, NIPR confirmations, reason-code determination, counsel clearance, producer copy and any DOI correspondence - into the repository under the writing company and state.
Apply the 5-years-after-termination-effective-date retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, termination effective date, reason code and NIPR transaction reference.
Record the repository reference on the case and close it.
checklist.done: each closed case is retained for 5 years and retrievable by NPN, reason code and NIPR transaction reference.

testing.step: Build the population of SC appointment and termination events
actions: Extract every South Carolina producer status change in the quarter from the producer master status history, with NPN, old status, new status and effective date.
Add HR leaver records for employed agents and Distribution contract-cancellation records so terminations that never reached the licensing desk are visible.
Add all SC applications written by producers with no active appointment on the application date, from the policy administration system.
Record the population with row counts, query text and run date, signed by the extractor.
testing.done: a signed event population covering status changes, HR leavers, contract cancellations and unappointed applications exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the event population to the NIPR transaction log
actions: Download the NIPR Gateway transaction history for South Carolina for the quarter, covering appointments, terminations and rejects.
Match on NPN plus company NAIC code plus effective date and list events with no matching NIPR transaction and transactions with no matching event.
Chase every unmatched row - an HR leaver with no termination transaction is a missed filing, and a NIPR termination with no internal case is an unlogged event.
Record the reconciliation and any residual differences in the workpaper before sampling.
testing.done: every internal event ties to a NIPR transaction and vice versa, with unmatched rows carried forward as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations, 100% of events already flagged late, and 100% of unappointed-application events.
Take 30 further events at random from the remainder using a recorded seed, for a minimum of 45 events in total.
Record population size, seed, selection rule and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Split the sample into appointment and termination subsamples because they carry different date maths.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of at least 45 events is drawn, including every for-cause and every already-late case.

testing.step: Recompute the 15-day appointment clock from source dates
actions: For each sampled appointment, take day zero from the source documents - the DocuSign envelope completion date and the earliest SC application date - not from the case header.
Recompute day zero plus 15 calendar days and compare it to the NIPR submission date on the transaction confirmation.
Record days late for every breach and list the SC applications and premium written between day zero and the appointment effective date.
Treat a case whose recorded day zero differs from the source documents as an exception even where the filing was timely.
testing.done: day zero is re-derived from source documents for every sampled appointment and days late are quantified.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day termination notice and 15-day producer copy clocks
actions: For each sampled termination, take the termination effective date from the contract cancellation or HR leaver record rather than the case header.
Recompute effective date plus 30 days and compare it to the NIPR termination submission date; record days late for each breach.
Recompute the NIPR submission date plus 15 days and compare it to the producer-copy send date evidenced on the case.
Confirm the copy went to the address of record shown on the PDB report at the time - a copy sent to a stale internal address does not satisfy the requirement.
testing.done: both clocks are recomputed from source dates for every sampled termination, with days late and address source recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the reason-code determination independently
actions: Read the underlying evidence for each sampled termination - complaint file, audit finding, premium account record, SIU referral - before looking at the filed code.
Reach an independent for-cause or not-for-cause conclusion and name the reason code you would have filed.
Compare to the filed code; a for-cause fact pattern filed as not for cause is a fail requiring an amended NIPR filing and a report to the Head of Compliance.
Confirm the filed narrative states only facts the evidence supports, and flag any speculative wording.
testing.done: each sampled termination has an independent reason-code conclusion, with mis-coded filings flagged for amendment.

testing.step: Trace each sampled event to its NIPR confirmation and PDB effect
actions: Open the NIPR transaction confirmation for each sampled event and check company NAIC code, NPN, effective date and lines of authority.
Run a current PDB report and confirm the appointment appears or has closed with the effective date the company filed.
Where a reject occurred, read the reject reason and confirm the resubmission kept the original effective date.
Capture both the NIPR confirmation and the PDB appointment section into the workpaper against the sample row.
testing.done: each sampled event traces to a NIPR confirmation and a matching PDB state, with rejects and resubmissions evidenced.

testing.step: Test the downstream cut-off on terminated producers
actions: For each sampled termination, check for SC new-business commission paid after the termination effective date.
Check for SC applications or endorsements written under the terminated NPN after the effective date in the policy administration system.
Confirm CRM, portal and policy admin access were revoked, taking the revocation date from the IAM record rather than the licensing case note.
Confirm the in-force book was reassigned to an appointed servicing producer and list any SC policies still orphaned at test date.
testing.done: no post-termination writing or commission is found, access revocation dates are IAM-evidenced, and orphaned policies are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, event type, statutory due date, actual filing date, days late and the business written in the gap.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (trigger not detected, wrong day zero, reject unworked, reason code wrong, producer copy missed, HR handoff broken) and a named owner.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether a late or amended filing needs an explanatory letter to the SC Department of Insurance.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries days late, business written in the gap, a root cause, an owner and a counsel decision on SC DOI notification.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute on-time percentages for the 15-day appointment, 30-day termination and 15-day producer-copy clocks against the 100% threshold.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with workpaper references behind each timeliness figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who staffs no part of the appointment desk and submitted none of the sampled transactions, sign the workpaper.
Report timeliness, mis-coded terminations and any SC DOI correspondence to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states on-time percentages per clock, the conclusion, and the committee reporting date.
