checklist.step: Harvest Arkansas expiration dates into the renewal calendar
actions: Run the monthly PDB extract for every NPN appointed by the writing company in Arkansas and read the Arkansas licence expiration date, licence class and lines of authority.
Load one renewal calendar row per producer per licence carrying NPN, licence number, expiration date, resident or non-resident status and the biennial cycle end.
Compare the extracted expiration date to the date held on the producer master and correct the master from PDB, never the reverse - PDB is the state's record.
List producers appointed in Arkansas with no Arkansas licence on PDB and hand them to the Producer Compliance Manager as an immediate exception.
checklist.done: the renewal calendar holds a PDB-sourced expiration date for every AR-appointed NPN, with unlicensed appointees escalated.

checklist.step: Map each producer onto the Arkansas biennial birth-month cycle
actions: For resident Arkansas producers, confirm the expiration falls on the biennial schedule keyed to the licensee's birth month and record the cycle start and end dates.

For non-resident producers, record that the Arkansas licence follows the company's non-resident renewal terms and that a home-state lapse will collapse it - and note the home-state expiration on the same row.
Record the business entity licence expirations separately, since an agency licence lapse stops every producer writing under it.
Flag any producer with two Arkansas licence records so duplicates are resolved with the Arkansas Insurance Department before renewal.
checklist.done: every row shows the correct Arkansas cycle dates, home-state expiration where relevant, and no unresolved duplicate licences.

checklist.step: Pull the current CE transcript for each producer in the window
actions: At T-120 days to expiration, retrieve each producer's Arkansas CE transcript from the state CE administrator's licensee portal using the licence number.
Transcribe onto the calendar row: total approved hours banked in the current biennium, ethics hours banked, and the reporting dates of each course.
Only count courses shown as reported and approved on the state transcript - a certificate held by the producer that the provider has not reported does not count toward the requirement.
Attach the dated transcript to the producer record as CE-<NPN>-AR-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf.
checklist.done: every producer in the 120-day window has a dated state CE transcript with banked total and ethics hours recorded.

checklist.step: Compute the CE gap and issue it to the producer
actions: Compute hours short as the Arkansas biennial requirement of 24 approved hours minus banked hours, and separately compute ethics hours short against the state-mandated ethics minimum.
Check for any line-specific requirement the producer's LOAs trigger, such as annuity suitability or long-term-care training, and add it to the gap statement.
Send each producer a written gap statement naming hours short, ethics hours short, the expiration date and the internal completion deadline set at T-45 days.
Copy the producer's Agency Relations Manager so distribution management owns the chase alongside licensing.
checklist.done: each producer holds a written gap statement naming total hours short, ethics hours short and a T-45 completion deadline.

checklist.step: Assign approved courses and track completion
actions: Assign courses only from the Arkansas Insurance Department approved course list, matching the producer's LOAs and their ethics shortfall.
Set the course due dates to the T-45 internal deadline and enable weekly reminders to the producer and their manager.
Track completion in the LMS and record the provider's state course number against each completion so it can be matched on the state transcript later.
Escalate any producer still short at T-60 to the Agency Relations Manager with the number of hours outstanding.
checklist.done: every short producer has AR-approved courses assigned with state course numbers tracked and a T-45 due date.

checklist.step: Confirm the state transcript, not the certificate, shows the hours
actions: At T-30 days, re-pull the Arkansas CE transcript for every producer in the window.
Confirm each completed course now appears as reported and approved, matching the state course numbers recorded at assignment.

Where a course was completed but not reported, chase the provider directly with the completion certificate and record the chase date - provider reporting lag is the most common cause of a failed renewal.
Mark the calendar row CE Complete only when the transcript shows the full hours including ethics.
checklist.done: every row is marked CE Complete against a re-pulled state transcript, with unreported courses chased to the provider.

checklist.step: Confirm any line-specific training obligations are satisfied
actions: List producers holding annuity, long-term care or flood lines of authority in Arkansas from the PDB extract.
Confirm the required product-specific training is on the transcript or in the carrier training record and is current for the cycle.
Where a producer sells annuities, confirm the annuity suitability training and any carrier-specific product training are both recorded before renewal.
Block the renewal row where line-specific training is missing rather than renewing and remediating later.
checklist.done: every line-specific training obligation is evidenced, or the renewal row is blocked until it is.

checklist.step: Submit the Arkansas licence renewal through the NIPR Gateway
actions: In the NIPR Gateway open Licence Renewal, select Arkansas and enter the NPN and licence number for each CE Complete row.
Answer the background and regulatory-action questions from the producer's current attestation, and stop the submission for referral where any answer changed.
Pay the Arkansas renewal fee and record the NIPR transaction reference, submission date and fee on the calendar row.
Submit no later than the internal target of 10 days before expiration so a reject can still be cured inside the cycle.
checklist.done: every CE Complete row is submitted through NIPR at least 10 days before expiration with the transaction reference recorded.

checklist.step: Confirm the renewal landed on the Producer Database
actions: Two business days after submission, re-pull the PDB report and confirm the Arkansas licence shows Active with the new expiration date.
Work every renewal reject by its reason code - CE not satisfied on the state record, fee failure, answer requiring review - and resubmit the same week.
Update the producer master and the renewal calendar with the new expiration date from PDB.
Attach the NIPR confirmation and the post-renewal PDB capture to the producer record.
checklist.done: PDB shows the renewed Arkansas licence with a new expiration date, captured against the producer record.

checklist.step: Suspend writing the moment a licence lapses
actions: Run the daily overdue queue of Arkansas licences past their expiration date with no confirmed renewal.
Set the producer master status to Suspended the same business day, which must cascade to the policy administration new-business edit and the commission platform.
Notify the producer and their Agency Relations Manager in writing that Arkansas solicitation and application-taking must stop immediately.
Open a lapse case recording the lapse start date so the exposure window is measured from day one.
checklist.done: every lapsed Arkansas producer is suspended the same business day with a lapse case open and the producer notified.

checklist.step: Quantify and clean up any business written during a lapse
actions: For each lapse case, extract Arkansas applications, binds, endorsements and renewals written under that NPN between the lapse start and the reinstatement date.
Quantify policy count, written premium and commission paid inside the window and record it on the lapse case.
Refer the book to the Producer Compliance Manager to reassign each affected policy to a currently licensed and appointed producer of record.
Take the commission clawback and policyholder-notification decision to Regulatory Counsel where any business was written.
checklist.done: every lapse case quantifies the policies, premium and commission written in the window with a counsel-cleared disposition.

checklist.step: Run the reinstatement route rather than a fresh application where possible
actions: Check the Arkansas Insurance Department reinstatement window and fee for a lapsed licence and record which route applies to the producer.
Complete the outstanding CE first, since Arkansas will not reinstate on unmet education, then submit the reinstatement with the penalty fee through the NIPR Gateway.
Where the reinstatement window has closed, submit a new Arkansas licence application including the examination requirement if it has been reimposed.
On reinstatement, re-submit the Arkansas appointment where it was terminated by the lapse, and confirm both on a fresh PDB report.
checklist.done: each lapsed producer is reinstated or re-licensed with CE cleared, and the appointment is restored and PDB-confirmed.

checklist.step: Keep PDB Alerts covering the whole Arkansas roster
actions: Reconcile the NIPR PDB Alerts subscription list to the appointed Arkansas roster monthly and add every missing NPN.
Include the home state of each non-resident Arkansas producer in the subscription so a home-state lapse is caught.
Confirm alerts create cases in the licensing work queue and that the previous month's alerts were all worked to closure.
Report the subscription coverage percentage to the Head of Compliance each month.
checklist.done: PDB Alerts cover 100% of the appointed Arkansas roster plus home states, with the prior month's alerts closed.

checklist.step: Report renewal-cycle status to distribution management
actions: Publish a weekly Arkansas renewal dashboard showing producers by bucket: CE Complete, hours short, renewal submitted, renewed, lapsed.
Break the hours-short bucket down by agency so managers can chase their own producers.
Show the in-force premium sitting behind each at-risk producer so the commercial cost of a lapse is visible.
Circulate the dashboard to the Head of Distribution and Head of Compliance each Monday through the renewal cycle.
checklist.done: a weekly dashboard shows every AR producer's renewal bucket with agency breakdown and in-force premium at risk.

checklist.step: Retain the renewal and CE evidence
actions: Move the cycle file - PDB extracts, dated CE transcripts, gap statements, LMS completions, NIPR renewal confirmations and lapse cases - into the repository under the writing company and biennial cycle.
Apply the 5-years-after-cycle-close retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, Arkansas licence number, expiration date and cycle.
Record the repository reference on the renewal calendar and close the cycle.
checklist.done: the cycle file is retained for 5 years and retrievable by NPN, licence number and cycle.

testing.step: Build the Arkansas expiration and application population
actions: Run an independent PDB extract for every NPN appointed in Arkansas and take every licence with an expiration date inside the period.
Extract every Arkansas application and bound policy in the period with application date and writing producer NPN from the policy administration system.
Add business entity licences with expirations in the period, since an agency lapse invalidates every producer writing under it.
Record both populations with row counts, query text and run date, signed by the extractor.
testing.done: a signed population of AR licence expirations, agency licences and AR applications exists, sourced from PDB directly.

testing.step: Reconcile the auditor's PDB extract to the renewal calendar
actions: Match the auditor's PDB extract to the operational renewal calendar on NPN plus licence number.
List producers on PDB with an expiration in the period that never appeared on the calendar - a missing row means the producer was never chased.
List calendar rows with no PDB match and resolve whether the producer is appointed under a different NPN or was never licensed.
Clear or carry forward every difference before sampling and record the reconciliation in the workpaper.
testing.done: the renewal calendar is proven complete against an independent PDB extract, with missing rows carried as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers who lapsed in the period, 100% of reinstatements and 100% of agency entity licence expirations.
Take 30 renewals at random from the remaining expirations using a recorded seed, for a minimum of 40 rows in total.
Record population size, seed, selection rule and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Separate producers holding annuity or long-term-care lines into a subsample for the line-specific training test.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of at least 40 rows is drawn covering every lapse, reinstatement and agency expiration.

testing.step: Re-pull the CE transcript and recompute the hours
actions: Retrieve each sampled producer's Arkansas CE transcript directly from the state CE administrator's portal using the licence number.
Recompute total approved hours and ethics hours banked in the biennium against the Arkansas 24-hour requirement and the state ethics minimum.
Compare to the CE Complete mark on the calendar row; a row marked complete on certificates rather than the state transcript is an exception.
For the annuity and long-term-care subsample, confirm the product-specific training appears on the transcript or the carrier training record.
testing.done: CE hours and ethics hours are recomputed from the state transcript for every sampled producer, with over-marks logged.

testing.step: Trace each renewal to a NIPR transaction dated before expiration
actions: Open the NIPR renewal transaction confirmation for each sampled row and read the submission date, fee and outcome.
Compare the submission date to the licence expiration date and record days early or late.
Confirm the current PDB report shows the licence Active with a new expiration date consistent with the biennial cycle.
Where a reject occurred, confirm it was cured before expiration; a cure after expiration is a lapse regardless of the final outcome.
testing.done: every sampled renewal traces to a NIPR confirmation and a PDB-confirmed new expiration, with days early or late recorded.

testing.step: Recompute the renewal-cycle date maths
actions: For each sampled producer, recompute the biennial cycle end from the birth-month schedule and compare it to the expiration date the calendar used.
Recompute the T-120, T-90, T-60, T-45 and T-30 milestone dates and check the alert log shows each one fired for that producer.
For non-resident producers, compare the Arkansas expiration to the home-state expiration and flag any row where the home state expires first without monitoring.
Record every mis-derived cycle date, since a wrong cycle end means every downstream reminder fired late.
testing.done: cycle ends and milestone dates are recomputed for every sampled producer and each alert firing is evidenced.

testing.step: Test whether any Arkansas business was written during a lapse
actions: Join the application population to the PDB licence validity dates and list every Arkansas application whose application date falls outside a valid licence period for that NPN.
Do the same for the agency entity licence, listing applications written under an agency whose licence had lapsed.
Quantify policy count, written premium and commission paid for each lapse window found.
Compare the result to the lapse cases the licensing team opened; unfound business written in a lapse is a control failure as well as a breach.
testing.done: every application written outside a valid licence period is identified and quantified, and compared to the lapse cases opened.

testing.step: Test the suspension and reinstatement controls
actions: For each sampled lapse, take the suspension timestamp from the producer master audit trail and compare it to the expiration date.
Confirm the suspension cascaded to the policy administration new-business edit and the commission platform on the same day, using those systems' own logs.
For each reinstatement, confirm CE was cleared before the reinstatement was submitted and that the Arkansas appointment was re-filed and PDB-confirmed.
List every manual override of the suspension with who applied it and the stated reason.
testing.done: suspensions are proven same-day and system-wide, reinstatements are CE-cleared, and every override is listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, licence number, expiration date, lapse period, premium and commission written in the lapse.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list (producer missing from calendar, CE not reported by provider, gap statement not issued, renewal submitted late, suspension delayed, home-state lapse unmonitored) and a named owner.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether business written in a lapse requires policyholder notification, commission clawback or an Arkansas Insurance Department self-report.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries the lapse period, premium at risk, a root cause, an owner and a counsel disposition.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time renewal percentage and the CE-evidenced percentage against the 100% thresholds and total the premium written during lapses.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with workpaper references behind each figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who runs no part of the renewal calendar and submitted none of the sampled renewals, sign the workpaper.
Report renewal timeliness, lapse exposure and any Arkansas Insurance Department correspondence to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states on-time renewal and CE percentages, lapse premium, the conclusion and the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the 18 U.S.C. 1033 screening gate for every person engaged in the business of insurance in Alaska - employees, producers and agency principals - and owns the 1033 written-consent applications made to the Alaska Division of Insurance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - 18 U.S.C. 1033(e) (prohibition on engaging in the business of insurance after a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust, absent the commissioner's written consent) and 18 U.S.C. 1034, read with Alaska Statutes Title 21 Chapter 27 producer licensing and character provisions and current Alaska Division of Insurance guidance; Alabama Title 27 and the Arkansas Insurance Code read for the adjacent rep states

In-scope processes.value: Pre-hire and pre-appointment screening: candidate and producer background checks, criminal-history adjudication against the dishonesty/breach-of-trust test, PDB and RIRS regulatory-action review, 1033 written-consent application, and the annual conviction re-attestation for the Alaska population

In-scope systems.value: Consumer reporting agency criminal-history searches (county, state and federal) plus sanctions and adverse-media screening; candidate flow in Greenhouse and employee records in the HRIS; producer regulatory actions from NIPR PDB/RIRS; adjudications filed in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: 1033 Screening and Consent Procedure - trigger population definition, FCRA-compliant disclosure and authorisation, search scope, the dishonesty/breach-of-trust adjudication test, the Alaska written-consent application route and the duty-restriction rules pending consent

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance, General Counsel and the Chief HR Officer; re-approved annually and on any change to Alaska Division of Insurance 1033 consent guidance or to state ban-the-box or fair-chance rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per hire and per producer appointment - the screening must clear before the person engages in the business of insurance in Alaska; a producer's duty to report a conviction or administrative action runs within 30 days of the event under the producer agreement; the FCRA pre-adverse-action notice must precede final action with a reasonable interval (5 business days is the working standard)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Requisition and appointment cases age daily and cannot advance to offer or appointment without a cleared screening flag; annual re-attestation campaigns fire on the Alaska population each January with reminders at day 14 and day 21; open 1033 consent applications alert every 30 days until decided

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed FCRA disclosure and authorisation, the consumer report, the adjudication memo, the pre-adverse and adverse-action notices, the Alaska 1033 consent application and the commissioner's written consent retained 7 years from separation or appointment termination, in a restricted-access folder

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any person found engaged in the business of insurance in Alaska with a disqualifying felony and no written consent is logged with the exposure period, the duties performed, the immediate removal action and the self-report decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every 1033 disqualification determination, every consent application filed with the Alaska Division of Insurance and every decision to remove or restrict a person already in role

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every person who began engaging in the business of insurance for the company in Alaska during the period - new hires into in-scope roles, newly appointed Alaska producers and newly onboarded agency principals - plus every RIRS regulatory action and self-reported conviction received in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any in-scope person engaged without a completed screening, or with a disqualifying felony and no written consent on file, is a fail; a single fail escalates to General Counsel and the Head of Compliance the same day

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per hire and per appointment; a monthly control check covers that month's starters and appointments and a documented quarterly test re-performs adjudications over the quarter's population, with an annual full-population re-attestation sweep

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside HR and the licensing desk and must have adjudicated none of the sampled screenings

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly 1033 screening test workpaper (starter and appointment population, screening re-performance, adjudication review, consent tracking, exceptions) in a restricted folder of the compliance evidence repository, access-limited to Compliance, Legal and Internal Audit

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Alaska in-scope population list with screening completion dates, adjudication outcomes and consent references, producible to the Alaska Division of Insurance within 5 business days, with underlying consumer reports released only through General Counsel

Regulator response path.value: Compliance Officer coordinates Alaska Division of Insurance inquiries; General Counsel clears every response and owns any voluntary disclosure of a person who worked while disqualified

checklist.step: Define who is engaged in the business of insurance in Alaska
actions: Read 18 U.S.C. 1033(e) with General Counsel and write the company's in-scope test: any person whose activities involve the transaction of insurance affecting interstate commerce for the Alaska book.

Apply the test to the job architecture and mark every job code in scope or out - underwriting, claims, actuarial, policy administration, producer-facing distribution, premium handling and their managers are in; unrelated corporate functions are out unless they touch insurance transactions.
Add every appointed Alaska producer, agency principal and designated responsible licensed producer to the in-scope population regardless of employment status.
Publish the in-scope job code list to HR and Talent Acquisition and diary a review each time the job architecture changes.
checklist.done: a published, counsel-agreed in-scope list names every job code and producer category caught by 1033 for Alaska.

checklist.step: Wire the screening gate into recruiting and onboarding
actions: Tag every requisition with an in-scope job code so the 1033 screening stage is inserted automatically into the hiring workflow.
Configure the offer stage so it cannot be completed while the screening stage is open, and route exceptions to the Compliance Officer rather than to the hiring manager.
Insert the Alaska-specific conviction question set into the application at the point state fair-chance rules permit it, not before.
Confirm each month that no in-scope requisition reached offer with the screening stage skipped.
checklist.done: in-scope requisitions carry a mandatory screening stage that blocks the offer, with monthly bypass checks run.

checklist.step: Take the FCRA disclosure and authorisation before any search runs
actions: Issue the standalone FCRA disclosure - a document containing nothing but the disclosure - together with the written authorisation and any Alaska and home-state summary of rights.
Collect the signed authorisation before ordering the consumer report, and record the signature date on the case.
Collect the same disclosure and authorisation from producers and agency principals through the onboarding pack, since 1033 does not stop at employees.
Store the signed documents in the restricted screening folder, not in the general personnel file.
checklist.done: a dated, standalone FCRA disclosure and signed authorisation exists for every in-scope person before any search is ordered.

checklist.step: Order the criminal-history search at the right scope
actions: Order through the consumer reporting agency: a SSN trace and address history, county criminal searches for every county of residence in the last seven years, statewide criminal searches where available, a federal district court search, and the national sex offender and sanctions lists.
Add the federal district search explicitly - most felonies involving dishonesty, such as mail and wire fraud, are federal and do not appear on county searches.
Include the Alaska statewide search wherever the person will work in or service the Alaska book.
Record the order date, the vendor reference and the exact search scope on the case so the scope can be re-performed later.
checklist.done: the search covers SSN trace, seven-year county history, statewide, federal district and sanctions lists, with scope recorded.

checklist.step: Screen producers through the Producer Database as well
actions: For every in-scope producer run a PDB report and read the Regulatory Actions (RIRS) section across all states.
Record each action's state, date, reason code and disposition, and obtain the consent order or final order behind any action involving fraud, misappropriation or unlicensed activity.
Cross-check the Alaska Division of Insurance enforcement actions page for orders that may not yet appear in RIRS.
Attach the dated PDB report and every retrieved order to the screening case.
checklist.done: every in-scope producer has a dated RIRS review with the underlying orders retrieved for dishonesty-related actions.

checklist.step: Adjudicate each hit against the dishonesty and breach-of-trust test
actions: For each criminal record returned, record the charge, statute, jurisdiction, disposition, conviction date and whether it was a felony as classified by the convicting jurisdiction.

Apply the two-part 1033 test in writing: was it a felony, and did it involve dishonesty or breach of trust - fraud, theft, embezzlement, forgery, perjury and false statements are in; many violence and drug offences are not.

Send borderline classifications - deferred adjudications, expungements, out-of-country convictions, youthful-offender dispositions - to General Counsel for a written call rather than deciding them at the desk.
Write the adjudication memo naming the record, the test applied and the outcome (no bar / bar absent consent) and sign and date it.
checklist.done: every criminal record carries a signed adjudication memo applying the felony and dishonesty tests explicitly.

checklist.step: Run the FCRA adverse-action sequence properly where a record drives the outcome
actions: Send the pre-adverse-action notice with a copy of the consumer report and the summary of rights before any decision is communicated.
Wait a reasonable interval - the standard here is 5 business days - for the person to dispute accuracy or supply context, and log anything they send.
Where the record is corrected by the vendor, re-adjudicate before proceeding, and record the corrected outcome.
Where the outcome stands, send the adverse-action notice naming the consumer reporting agency and the right to dispute, and file both notices on the case.
checklist.done: pre-adverse and adverse notices are sent in sequence with a documented 5-business-day interval and any dispute logged.

checklist.step: Restrict duties immediately where a bar is identified
actions: On a bar determination, stop the person from performing any in-scope activity for the Alaska book on the same business day.
For producers, suspend the Alaska appointment status and the writing number so no further Alaska business can be submitted.
For employees already in role, move them out of in-scope duties or place them on paid suspension while consent is pursued - continuing in role without consent is the offence 1033 creates.
Record the restriction date, the duties removed and who authorised it on the case.
checklist.done: every barred person is out of in-scope Alaska duties the same business day, with the restriction dated and authorised.

checklist.step: Build and file the Alaska 1033 written-consent application
actions: Confirm with the Alaska Division of Insurance the form, evidence and fee its consent process requires, and record the guidance version relied on.

Assemble the package: the person's written statement, certified court records showing the charge and disposition, evidence of sentence completion and restitution, character references, the proposed role and its supervision plan, and the company's own risk assessment.
Draft the application setting out why the proposed duties do not create an unacceptable risk, and have the person sign their statement.
File the application with the Division, record the filing date and reference, and set a 30-day follow-up cycle until a decision issues.
checklist.done: a complete consent application is filed with the Alaska Division of Insurance with a filing reference and a 30-day follow-up cycle.

checklist.step: Track the consent decision and enforce its conditions
actions: Log the Division's written consent, denial or conditional consent against the case with its date and any conditions attached.
Where consent is conditional - limited lines, supervision, reporting - write the conditions into the person's role profile and system entitlements so they are enforced rather than remembered.
Where consent is denied, terminate the appointment or move the person permanently out of in-scope duties and record the action date.
Diary any expiry or review date the consent carries so it is renewed before it lapses.
checklist.done: each consent outcome is recorded, its conditions are enforced in entitlements, and any review date is diarised.

checklist.step: Collect the annual conviction and action re-attestation
actions: Each January issue the attestation to the full Alaska in-scope population asking about felony convictions, pending charges and administrative actions since the last attestation.
Chase non-responders at day 14 and day 21 and escalate anyone outstanding at day 30 to their manager and the Head of Compliance.
Route every positive response into the adjudication process the same week rather than holding it to a batch review.
Record completion rates and positive responses and report both to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the annual attestation reaches 100% of the Alaska in-scope population with every positive response adjudicated.

checklist.step: Keep ongoing monitoring running between screenings
actions: Keep every appointed Alaska producer on NIPR PDB Alerts so a new regulatory action creates a licensing case automatically.
Run a quarterly re-screen of sanctions and enforcement lists across the in-scope population through the consumer reporting agency.
Enforce the producer agreement's 30-day self-reporting duty by chasing any action found on PDB that the producer did not report, and record the failure to report.
Feed every hit into the adjudication process with the same memo standard as a pre-hire screen.
checklist.done: alerts and quarterly re-screens run across the in-scope population and every hit reaches adjudication.

checklist.step: Train the people who make the call
actions: Assign an annual 1033 adjudication module to Compliance, HR and Licensing staff covering the felony and dishonesty tests, FCRA sequencing and the consent route.
Include worked examples of the traps: federal fraud convictions missing from county searches, deferred adjudications, and out-of-state records surfacing only on the SSN trace.
Assign a shorter awareness module to hiring managers covering why an offer cannot be made before clearance.
Record completions and withhold adjudication authority from anyone who has not completed the module.
checklist.done: everyone with adjudication authority has completed the current 1033 module and completions are recorded.

checklist.step: Restrict access to the screening evidence
actions: Hold consumer reports, adjudication memos and court records in a restricted folder with access limited to named Compliance, Legal and Internal Audit users.
Keep the screening record out of the general personnel file so line managers cannot read criminal history.
Run a quarterly access review of the folder and remove anyone who has changed role.
Log every access to a consumer report so a disclosure can be traced.
checklist.done: screening evidence sits in a named-access folder with quarterly access reviews and an access log.

checklist.step: Retain the screening and consent evidence
actions: File the complete case - disclosure and authorisation, consumer report, PDB/RIRS review, adjudication memo, adverse-action notices, consent application and the Division's decision - under the person and the writing company.
Apply the 7-years-from-separation-or-appointment-termination retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by person, NPN where applicable, adjudication outcome and consent reference.
Record the repository reference on the case and close it.
checklist.done: each screening case is retained for 7 years post-separation and retrievable by person, outcome and consent reference.

testing.step: Build the Alaska in-scope population for the period
actions: Extract every hire, internal transfer and rehire in the period whose job code sits on the published in-scope list and who touches the Alaska book.
Extract every Alaska producer appointment and agency principal onboarded in the period from the producer master.
Add contingent workers, contractors and outsourced-service staff performing in-scope duties, since 1033 follows the activity and not the payroll.
Record the population with row counts, query text and run date, signed by the extractor.
testing.done: a signed in-scope population covering employees, producers, principals and contingent workers exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the screening case log
actions: Match every population row to a screening case on person identifier or NPN.
List rows with no screening case at all, and cases whose completion date falls after the person's start date or appointment effective date.
Chase each unmatched row with HR and Licensing and confirm whether the person actually performed in-scope duties.
Treat any person who started in-scope work before screening completion as an automatic exception, no judgement applied.
testing.done: every in-scope person ties to a screening case completed before their start or appointment date, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of screenings that returned any criminal record, 100% of producers with a RIRS action, and 100% of open or granted 1033 consents.
Take 25 clear screenings at random from the remainder using a recorded seed, for a minimum of 35 cases in total.
Record population size, seed, selection rule and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Handle the sample in the restricted workpaper folder throughout, given the personal data involved.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of at least 35 cases is drawn covering every record hit, RIRS action and consent case.

testing.step: Re-perform the search scope test
actions: For each sampled case read the consumer reporting agency order detail and confirm the scope actually ordered: SSN trace, county searches for every address in the seven-year history, statewide searches, federal district search and sanctions lists.
Compare the counties searched to the address history returned by the SSN trace and list any residence county that was never searched.
Confirm the federal district search ran - its absence is the single most common way a dishonesty felony is missed.
Log every scope shortfall as an exception even where the report came back clear.
testing.done: search scope is re-performed against the address history for every sampled case, with missed counties and searches listed.

testing.step: Re-adjudicate the record hits independently
actions: Read the underlying court record for each sampled hit and classify it yourself: felony or misdemeanour as the convicting jurisdiction classified it, and dishonesty or breach of trust or neither.
Reach your own bar or no-bar conclusion before opening the adjudication memo.
Compare to the recorded outcome; a correct outcome resting on an unstated or wrong test is still an exception.
Pay particular attention to deferred adjudications, expungements and pleas, where the memo must show the reasoning rather than a bare conclusion.
testing.done: every sampled record hit has an independent bar/no-bar conclusion compared against the original memo.

testing.step: Trace consent applications to a Division decision and enforced conditions
actions: For each barred person, retrieve the Alaska 1033 consent application, its filing reference and the Division's written decision.
Confirm no in-scope Alaska duty was performed between the bar determination and the written consent, using system access logs and, for producers, the application and commission records.
For conditional consents, test that each condition is actually enforced in entitlements and role profile rather than only recorded on the case.
Where consent was denied, confirm the removal or termination date and that no in-scope activity followed it.
testing.done: each barred person has a traced Division decision with a proven duty gap and enforced conditions.

testing.step: Test the FCRA sequencing and intervals
actions: For every adverse outcome in the sample, confirm the standalone disclosure pre-dates the report order date.
Recompute the interval between the pre-adverse-action notice and the adverse-action notice and compare it to the 5-business-day standard.
Confirm the consumer report and summary of rights were enclosed with the pre-adverse notice.
Log any dispute the person raised and confirm a re-adjudication happened where the vendor corrected the record.
testing.done: disclosure ordering and the pre-adverse to adverse interval are recomputed for every adverse outcome in the sample.

testing.step: Test the ongoing monitoring and re-attestation coverage
actions: Reconcile the NIPR PDB Alerts subscription list to the appointed Alaska producer roster and list uncovered NPNs.
Take every RIRS action that appeared in the period and confirm each produced an adjudication case within a week of the alert.
Compare the annual attestation completion list to the full in-scope population and list non-responders still outstanding.
Test five producer-reported actions against the 30-day self-reporting duty and record any late or absent self-report.
testing.done: alert coverage, alert-to-adjudication turnaround and attestation completion are each measured with gaps listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the person or NPN, the in-scope duty performed, the exposure period and the screening or consent gap.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list (job code not tagged in scope, offer made before clearance, search scope short, adjudication test unstated, consent not pursued, condition not enforced, attestation not returned) and a named owner.
For any person who performed in-scope Alaska duties while barred, decide with General Counsel on immediate removal and on voluntary disclosure to the Alaska Division of Insurance.
Handle every issue record in the restricted tracker view given the personal data involved, and carry open items into the next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has an owner, root cause, exposure period and, where a bar was breached, a General Counsel disclosure decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute screening-before-start completion percentage and adjudication accuracy against the zero-tolerance threshold.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with restricted workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the Internal Auditor, who sits outside HR and licensing and adjudicated none of the sampled cases, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any bar breaches to the Compliance Committee in a confidential session and file the workpaper in the restricted repository folder.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states screening completion, adjudication accuracy, the conclusion and the confidential reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly reconciliation of the internal Hawaii producer roster to the state appointment record held in the NIPR Producer Database, and owns the break-clearance backlog

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Hawaii Revised Statutes Chapter 431 Article 9A (producer licensing, appointment and termination) read with current Hawaii Insurance Division producer licensing memoranda on appointment renewal and fees; Iowa Insurance Code and N.J. Statutes Titles 17 and 17B read for the adjacent rep states

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly three-way reconciliation of the Hawaii producer roster: internal producer master versus NIPR PDB licence and appointment data versus commission payments and written business, followed by break classification, ageing and clearance

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway PDB reports and appointment extracts as the state record; producer master in the agency/producer management system; payment data from the billing/commission platform; the reconciliation itself assembled in the enterprise data warehouse and published in Power BI

Compliance procedure documented.value: Hawaii Producer Roster Reconciliation Procedure - quarter-end extract timing, NPN key matching rules, the six break categories, ageing bands, clearance owners and the escalation path for breaks touching written business

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance and the Head of Distribution; re-approved annually and whenever the Hawaii Insurance Division changes appointment renewal mechanics or fee cycles

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly - extracts frozen within 5 business days of quarter end, breaks classified within 10 business days, clearance actions raised within 20 business days, and the signed reconciliation issued within 30 calendar days of quarter end; Hawaii appointment renewal invoices settled inside the Division's published renewal window

Deadline reminders configured.value: Quarter-end calendar tasks at day 5 (extract freeze), day 10 (classification), day 20 (clearance raised) and day 30 (sign-off), with any break older than two quarters escalating automatically to the Head of Compliance

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Frozen extracts, the matched reconciliation file, the break register with dispositions and the signed reconciliation certificate retained 5 years from the quarter end

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every break where a producer wrote Hawaii business or was paid commission without a current licence and active appointment is logged with policy count, premium, commission and the clawback, reassignment and self-report disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the quarterly reconciliation certificate and every disposition on a break that touched written Hawaii business

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full Hawaii producer roster at quarter end, the full NIPR PDB Hawaii appointment extract for the writing company, all Hawaii commission payments in the quarter and all Hawaii applications and bound policies in the quarter

Pass/fail thresholds.value: The roster must reconcile to the state record with zero unexplained breaks; zero tolerance on breaks where business was written or commission paid, and no break may age beyond two quarters - a single aged or business-touching break fails the control

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; the reconciliation runs every quarter end and the independent verification test re-performs the match and the break population for the same quarter before the certificate is signed

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not prepare the reconciliation, maintain the producer master or process Hawaii appointments

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly Hawaii roster reconciliation workpaper (frozen extracts, match file, break register, re-performance notes, exceptions, certificate) in the compliance evidence repository under the writing company and quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed quarterly reconciliation certificate with the Hawaii appointed-producer roster, break register and dispositions, producible to the Hawaii Insurance Division within 5 business days of a market conduct request

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers Hawaii Insurance Division roster and appointment inquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears any response disclosing business written by an unappointed producer

checklist.step: Freeze the internal Hawaii producer roster at quarter end
actions: Within 5 business days of quarter end, extract every producer and agency flagged active for Hawaii with NPN, legal name, licence number, lines of authority, appointment status, appointment effective date and agency hierarchy.
Take the extract as at the quarter-end date rather than as at run date so later status changes cannot move the baseline.
Save the file read-only as HI-roster-<yyyy-qq>-frozen.csv with the row count and run timestamp recorded on the reconciliation case.
Have the extract signed as complete by the person who ran it, with the query attached.
checklist.done: a read-only, signed Hawaii roster extract as at quarter end exists with row count and query recorded.

checklist.step: Pull the state's own appointment record from the Producer Database
actions: In the NIPR Gateway request the PDB appointment extract for the writing company's NAIC company code, filtered to Hawaii, covering every appointed NPN.
Include for each NPN: Hawaii licence number, licence status, licence expiration date, lines of authority, appointment status and appointment effective date.
Save the file read-only as HI-PDB-<yyyy-qq>.csv alongside the roster extract and record the NIPR request reference.
Treat this file as the state record - where it disagrees with the internal roster, the internal roster is what changes.
checklist.done: a read-only PDB Hawaii appointment extract for the correct NAIC code sits alongside the roster with its NIPR reference.

checklist.step: Pull the money and the business alongside the two rosters
actions: Extract every Hawaii commission payment in the quarter by NPN with payment date, amount, policy number and commission type (new business, renewal, override).
Extract from the policy administration system every Hawaii application, bind, endorsement and renewal in the quarter with the writing NPN and application date.
Include agency-level overrides so a payment routed to an agency rather than an individual cannot escape the match.
Record row counts and totals for both extracts on the reconciliation case.
checklist.done: commission payments and written business for the quarter are extracted by NPN with counts and totals recorded.

checklist.step: Match the four files on the National Producer Number
actions: Load all four extracts and join them on NPN as the single key - never on name, which fails on married names, suffixes and agency trading styles.
Report NPN data quality first: blanks, non-numeric values, duplicates and NPNs appearing on more than one producer master record.
Where an internal record has no NPN, look it up on the PDB by licence number and correct the master before matching, logging the correction.
Produce the matched file with one row per NPN carrying roster status, PDB licence and appointment status, commission paid and business written.
checklist.done: a single matched file keyed on NPN exists, with all key-quality defects listed and corrected before matching.

checklist.step: Classify every difference into a fixed break category
actions: Classify each non-matching row into one of six categories: (1) on roster as appointed, not appointed on PDB; (2) appointed on PDB, absent or inactive on roster; (3) appointed but Hawaii licence expired or inactive; (4) appointed for lines of authority the producer does not hold; (5) terminated on roster but still appointed on PDB; (6) paid commission or wrote business with no active licence and appointment.
Never open a seventh category called other - an unclassifiable row goes to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day.
Tag every category 1, 3, 4 and 6 break with the policy count, premium and commission attached to that NPN in the quarter.
Record the break count and value by category on the reconciliation case.
checklist.done: every difference sits in one of the six named categories with the business and commission exposure attached.

checklist.step: Age each break and set the escalation
actions: Match this quarter's break register to the prior quarter's to identify repeats and set the age in quarters on each row.
Band the register: new, one quarter old, two quarters old, older than two quarters.
Escalate anything older than two quarters to the Head of Compliance with a written explanation of why it has not cleared.
Escalate every category 6 break to the Producer Compliance Manager on the day it is identified, regardless of age.
checklist.done: every break carries an age in quarters, and aged and category 6 breaks are escalated with a written explanation.

checklist.step: Clear the category 1 breaks by appointing or stopping the producer
actions: For each producer marked appointed internally but not appointed on PDB, confirm on a fresh PDB report that the gap is real and not an extract timing artefact.
Where the producer is genuinely writing, submit the Hawaii appointment through the NIPR Gateway immediately and record the transaction reference and effective date.
Where the producer should not be writing, set the roster status to not appointed and close the writing number the same day.
Quantify and hand off any Hawaii business written while the gap was open to the exception process.
checklist.done: every category 1 break is either appointed in NIPR or stopped on the roster, with gap business quantified.

checklist.step: Clear the category 2 and 5 breaks by terminating the state record
actions: For each NPN appointed on PDB but inactive or terminated internally, confirm the internal termination date and the reason code recorded.
Submit the Hawaii termination through the NIPR Gateway with the correct reason code and the true termination effective date, and send the producer their copy.

Where no internal termination exists, decide with the Agency Relations Manager whether the producer is genuinely active - a producer appointed on PDB and unknown internally is a control failure worth its own root cause.
Confirm on a re-pulled PDB report that the appointment has closed and record the transaction reference.
checklist.done: every PDB appointment with no active internal producer is terminated in NIPR and confirmed closed on a re-pull.

checklist.step: Clear the licence and line-of-authority breaks
actions: For category 3, suspend the producer's Hawaii writing number the same day and put them into the renewal or reinstatement route with the CE requirement cleared first.
For category 4, either remove the unsupported product from the producer's authorised list or have them obtain the Hawaii line of authority, then correct the appointment lines in NIPR.
Notify the Agency Relations Manager and the producer in writing of the restriction and what must happen to lift it.
Re-pull the PDB after each correction and confirm the licence status and appointed lines now agree with the roster.
checklist.done: expired-licence producers are suspended and line mismatches corrected in NIPR, confirmed on a re-pulled PDB.

checklist.step: Deal with the money on the category 6 breaks
actions: For each producer paid or writing without a valid licence and appointment, total the commission paid and the premium written inside the invalid window.
Apply the producer agreement's forfeiture clause where it bites, raise the clawback and record the recovery plan.
Suspend further payment on that NPN until the roster and PDB agree, and confirm the suspension is system-enforced rather than a manual hold.
Refer the affected policies to Distribution for reassignment to a licensed and appointed Hawaii producer of record.
checklist.done: commission paid in invalid windows is quantified, clawed back or forfeited, payment is suspended and policies reassigned.

checklist.step: Reconcile the Hawaii appointment renewal invoice into the same cycle
actions: When the Hawaii Insurance Division appointment renewal invoice is published, download the invoiced NPN list from the NIPR Gateway.
Match the invoice to the reconciled roster and mark each line renew or terminate, using the same break register so the two exercises cannot disagree.
Submit the terminations before the renewal payment date so the company does not pay renewal fees on producers it is about to terminate.
Pay the renewals, then confirm on a PDB re-pull that renewed appointments carry the new period and terminated ones are closed.
checklist.done: the Hawaii renewal invoice is reconciled to the same break register, non-writers terminated first and the outcome PDB-confirmed.

checklist.step: Fix the causes, not only the breaks
actions: Group the quarter's breaks by root cause: appointment never submitted, NIPR reject unworked, termination never filed, PDB alert not actioned, producer master not updated from PDB, NPN key defect.
Raise a remediation issue per root cause with an owner and a due date, rather than only closing individual rows.
Where the same root cause appears in two consecutive quarters, require a documented process or system change rather than a repeat clean-up.
Report the top three root causes and their remediation status to the Head of Compliance each quarter.
checklist.done: each recurring root cause has an owned remediation issue and repeat causes carry a process or system change.

checklist.step: Publish the reconciliation result to distribution and compliance
actions: Publish the Hawaii reconciliation dashboard showing roster count, PDB appointment count, break count and value by category, and ageing bands.
Break the register down by agency so each Agency Relations Manager sees and owns their own producers' breaks.
Show premium and commission at risk on category 6 so the commercial consequence is visible alongside the compliance one.
Circulate to the Head of Distribution and Head of Compliance within 30 days of quarter end.
checklist.done: a published dashboard shows counts, break values by category and ageing, broken down by agency, inside 30 days.

checklist.step: Sign the quarterly reconciliation certificate
actions: Read the reconciliation summary, break register and disposition status before signing anything.
Confirm zero unexplained breaks remain, that every category 6 break has a disposition, and that nothing has aged beyond two quarters without an approved plan.
Sign and date the certificate stating that the Hawaii roster agrees to the state appointment record subject to the listed breaks.
Refuse to sign where the break register is incomplete, and record the refusal and its reason on the case.
checklist.done: a dated certificate is signed stating agreement subject to a complete, dispositioned break register.

checklist.step: Retain the reconciliation evidence
actions: File the frozen extracts, matched file, break register, clearance evidence, NIPR transaction confirmations and the signed certificate under the writing company and quarter.
Apply the 5-years-from-quarter-end retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by quarter, NPN, break category and NIPR transaction reference.
Record the repository reference on the reconciliation case and close the quarter.
checklist.done: the quarter's reconciliation file is retained for 5 years and retrievable by quarter, NPN and break category.

testing.step: Rebuild the population independently from source
actions: Run the auditor's own PDB Hawaii appointment extract for the writing company's NAIC code rather than using the licensing team's file.
Take an independent Hawaii roster extract from the producer master as at quarter end and an independent Hawaii commission extract for the quarter.
Compare row counts and totals to the frozen files used in the operational reconciliation and list any difference.
A material difference between the auditor's PDB pull and the operational one means the wrong company code or filter was used and is reported before anything else.
testing.done: independent PDB, roster and commission extracts exist and their counts are compared to the operational files.

testing.step: Reconcile the operational reconciliation to the auditor's rebuild
actions: Re-run the NPN match on the auditor's extracts using the documented matching rules.
Compare the auditor's break population to the operational break register and list breaks the operational run missed and breaks it raised that do not exist.
Investigate every missed break to its cause - excluded status codes, date filters, agency-level rows dropped, NPN blanks silently excluded.
Record the completeness result as a percentage of the auditor's break population that the operational register captured.
testing.done: the operational break register's completeness is measured against an independently rebuilt break population.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of category 6 breaks, 100% of breaks aged beyond one quarter and 100% of breaks marked cleared in the quarter.
Take 25 matched rows at random from the clean population using a recorded seed to test that clean rows really are clean, for a minimum of 40 rows.
Record population size, seed, selection rule and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Include at least five agency-level rows so override payments are covered.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of at least 40 rows is drawn covering all category 6, aged and cleared breaks plus clean rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the break classification
actions: For each sampled break, read the roster status, PDB licence and appointment status, commission and business data and classify it yourself into the six categories.
Compare to the recorded category; a mis-classified break usually means the wrong clearance route was taken, so record the downstream consequence too.

For sampled clean rows, verify independently that the roster appointment status, PDB appointment status and licence status all agree - a clean row hiding a licence expiry is the worst finding available.
Log every disagreement with the underlying field values quoted.
testing.done: every sampled break is independently classified and every sampled clean row is independently proven clean.

testing.step: Verify each break clearance in the state system
actions: For each break marked cleared, retrieve the NIPR appointment or termination transaction confirmation and read its date, reason code and effective date.
Run a current PDB report on the NPN and confirm the state record now reflects the intended state - appointed, terminated, or lines corrected.
Reject any clearance evidenced only by an internal status change; the break is not cleared until the state record moves.
Capture the PDB screen against each sample row.
testing.done: every cleared break is proven against a current PDB report, not against an internal status flag alone.

testing.step: Recompute the exposure on category 6 breaks
actions: For each category 6 NPN, take the licence and appointment validity windows from PDB and list every Hawaii application, bind and endorsement outside those windows.
Recompute premium written and commission paid inside the invalid window and compare to the figure on the break register.
Confirm the clawback or forfeiture was actually raised in the commission platform and trace the recovery status.
Confirm each affected policy was reassigned to a licensed and appointed Hawaii producer of record, and list any still orphaned.
testing.done: exposure on every category 6 break is independently recomputed and the clawback and reassignment are traced.

testing.step: Test the timeliness of the reconciliation cycle itself
actions: Take the extract freeze timestamp, classification completion date, clearance-raised date and certificate signature date from the case record.
Recompute each against the day 5, day 10, day 20 and day 30 targets from quarter end and record days late for each milestone.
Confirm the frozen extracts are genuinely read-only and unmodified since the freeze by comparing file hashes or version history.
A reconciliation signed on time but built on extracts amended after the freeze is reported as a control failure.
testing.done: each cycle milestone is recomputed against its target and extract immutability since the freeze is proven.

testing.step: Test root-cause remediation and repeat breaks
actions: Compare this quarter's break register to the prior two quarters and list NPNs appearing in all three.
For each repeat root cause, open the remediation issue and check whether a process or system change was made or only a clean-up performed.
Confirm the PDB Alerts subscription covers 100% of the appointed Hawaii roster, since uncovered NPNs are a standing cause of repeat breaks.
Record repeat-break count and the proportion of root causes with a delivered structural fix.
testing.done: repeat breaks are quantified and each recurring root cause is shown to have a delivered fix or is reported as unremediated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, break category, quarters aged, premium and commission at risk and what the reconciliation missed or mis-handled.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list (extract filter wrong, NPN key defect, classification error, clearance not filed with the state, ageing not escalated, alerts not covering the roster) and a named owner.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether any Hawaii business written by an unappointed producer requires policyholder notification or a Hawaii Insurance Division disclosure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's reconciliation as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a counsel decision where business was written.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute break-register completeness, classification accuracy, clearance verification rate and total premium and commission at risk.

State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with workpaper references behind each measure, and withhold the quarterly certificate where the conclusion is ineffective.
Have the Internal Auditor, who neither prepares the reconciliation nor maintains the producer master, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion, aged breaks and any Hawaii Insurance Division disclosure to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states completeness, accuracy, exposure at risk, the conclusion and the committee reporting date.
